metrics.interpretation: Tracks the share of population with electricity access. This is useful context for EISD accessibility but is not asserted to be the official SOC1 formula.
metrics.label: Access to electricity
metrics.source_semantics: World Bank indicator semantics and source metadata control interpretation.

metrics.interpretation: Tracks renewable energy in total final energy consumption; denominator and classification follow the source indicator.
metrics.label: Renewable energy consumption
metrics.source_semantics: Related to EISD renewable share, but not substituted for the unavailable official EISD methodology sheet.

metrics.interpretation: Tracks net energy imports relative to energy use. Negative values may indicate net exports and must not be clamped or reinterpreted.
metrics.label: Energy imports, net
metrics.source_semantics: Related to EISD import dependency; source definition remains authoritative for this observation series.

metrics.interpretation: Country-level energy-use intensity normalized by population, retaining the source's primary-energy accounting conventions.
metrics.label: Energy use per capita
metrics.source_semantics: Related to EISD ECO1 without claiming official EISD methodological equivalence.
metrics.unit: kg of oil equivalent per capita

metrics.interpretation: Tracks fossil-fuel share of total energy use and should be read alongside other fuel-mix metrics rather than as a standalone sustainability score.
metrics.label: Fossil fuel energy consumption
metrics.source_semantics: Source indicator classification and accounting basis control the observation.

metrics.interpretation: Tracks renewable output in electricity generation; it is distinct from renewable share of total final energy consumption.
metrics.label: Renewable electricity output
metrics.source_semantics: Electricity-output share must not be substituted for whole-energy-system renewable share.

metrics.interpretation: Tracks per-capita electricity consumption; it is narrower than total energy use per capita.
metrics.label: Electric power consumption per capita
metrics.source_semantics: Electricity and total-energy metrics remain separate accounting scopes.

metrics.interpretation: Tracks electricity transmission and distribution losses relative to output as a system-efficiency context metric.
metrics.label: Electric power transmission and distribution losses
metrics.source_semantics: Related to EISD conversion/distribution efficiency without asserting formula equivalence.

metrics.interpretation: Tracks economic output per unit of energy use. It is the reciprocal-style productivity framing of energy intensity, not the same quantity as energy use per unit of GDP.
metrics.label: GDP per unit of energy use
metrics.source_semantics: Do not invert or compare against ECO2 without preserving price basis, energy basis, and methodology.
metrics.unit: constant 2021 PPP $ per kg of oil equivalent

contract.country_code_format: ISO-like 2- or 3-letter code accepted by source provider
contract.default_window: 15 years ending in the runtime current year
contract.freshness_policy: report latest observed year and lag; never relabel as current-year data

sources.coverage: Country/region time-series indicators surfaced through World Development Indicators and related World Bank datasets.
sources.label: World Bank Indicators API v2 — energy indicators
sources.license_context: Indicator-specific source and licensing metadata must be preserved; do not infer one universal license from the API transport layer.
sources.note: The v2 Indicators API is used as the first live global-energy connector because it requires no API key. Selected metrics are explicit source codes, not Sustainable Catalyst estimates.
sources.update_context: Observation years differ by indicator and country; the API exposes historical time series and metadata. v0.8.0 preserves each returned observation year.

sources.coverage: Curated electricity generation, electricity demand, power-sector emissions, carbon intensity, and installed-capacity datasets.
sources.label: Ember Energy Data API
sources.license_context: Ember documents its API data under CC BY 4.0; attribution must be preserved.
sources.note: v0.8.0 records the connector contract but does not add or require an Ember API key, so no live Ember request is executed by this release.
sources.update_context: Temporal coverage and freshness vary by endpoint; yearly and monthly datasets are available for supported series.

sources.coverage: Hierarchical energy datasets including international and U.S. energy series, depending on route and facets.
sources.label: U.S. Energy Information Administration API v2
sources.license_context: Reuse terms are source-specific and must be retained with dataset metadata.
sources.note: The API v2 contract is registered, but v0.8.0 does not require an EIA API key and does not execute the connector.
sources.update_context: Dataset periodicity and update cadence vary by route; metadata is route-specific.

sources.coverage: Country-level energy, efficiency, prices, emissions, and related energy-system datasets through IEA data products and explorers.
sources.label: International Energy Agency data explorers
sources.license_context: License and access terms are dataset-specific and must be checked before automated reuse.
sources.note: v0.8.0 recognizes IEA as a primary energy-data authority but does not assume a universal public API or universal reuse terms across IEA products.
sources.update_context: Freshness and access mode are dataset-specific; some current data products expose recent 2026 updates.
